::: {.callout-note}
**This page is for the facilitator.** It is left out of the navbar, so nothing on the site links to it. The track pages under `tracks/` are participant-facing and contain no instructor guidance, which is collected here and in the run sheets of the [facilitator guide of the case](housing-guide.qmd).
:::

## The formats

The facilitator chooses the format and, for a one-day course, its focus; participants do not choose, and the opening page describes the formats without offering a choice. Each track is an ordered route through pages that already exist on the site, with a docked sidebar of its own (`_sidebar.yml`) and a slides page embedding the deck on which it runs. Each part page of a track carries the instructions for that part, with buttons into the page where the work is done, and the previous and next links at its foot follow the order of the sidebar. The timings of each step are kept in the run sheets of the facilitator guide, and the participant pages give only the length of each part. Name the track of a delivery in `delivery.track` of `_variables.yml`, and the callout of the opening page links it; the navbar then shows a participant the last track page that they opened.

| Format | Track | Deck |
|---|---|---|
| Short session, browser only | `tracks/housing-short/` | `slides/housing-short.qmd` |
| One day, open science | `tracks/housing-one-day-open-science/` | `slides/housing-one-day-open-science.qmd` |
| One day, data tools | `tracks/housing-one-day-data-tools/` | `slides/housing-one-day-data-tools.qmd` |
| One day, methods | `tracks/housing-one-day-methods/` | `slides/housing-one-day-methods.qmd` |
| Self-study | `tracks/self-study/` | `slides/housing-one-day-methods.qmd` |

**What each one-day focus keeps.** The open-science day takes the paper, the five analysts, the estimand statement, the reproduction of one reanalysis chosen by each participant and the replication with new data, and ends on what a preregistration fixes, with the block read and filled in but not run; it has no menu, no class chart and no submissions. The data-tools day practises R, the IDE, a Quarto report, data management and version control on the data of the case, with the reproduction as the target that the code works towards; it has no menu, no class chart and no submissions. The methods day puts the robustness exercise at the centre: the menu, the class chart with its submissions, the curve of the claim and the declared analysis. All three are taught mainly in the browser lab of the case, with the workspace as an option for those who have installed R.

## The browser lab

The browser lab is a page that runs R in the tab of the browser and holds the five tasks of the exercise beside the workspace. It is live: it loads the data of the case, about 100 KB of emails, and runs the code of the tasks on them, each fit in a fraction of a second, so the short session and the one-day courses are taught in it. The causal-graph task prints the answers that the pipeline computed with dagitty for the graphs that the cell offers, because dagitty cannot run in the tab; any other graph goes to the workspace.

## The decks

The decks are assembled from one pool of segments: the case-neutral segments of `slides/_segments/shared/` and the segments of the case in `slides/_segments/housing/`, whose setup chunk comes after the shared one and gives the shared segments the addresses of the case. A deck is a list of `{{< include >}}` lines with its own agenda, aims and part dividers.

**How the optional runs are switched.** In the segment files, every slide of an optional run is marked with `.deepdive` and a `run` attribute (`tools`, `r`, `methods`, `multiverse`). A deck lists the runs that belong to its main flow under `core-runs:` in its YAML, and `slides/core-runs.lua` strips the `.deepdive` mark from those headings, so `nav-tools.html` neither hides them on the `d` key nor badges them as optional. A run that is not listed stays optional: it is hidden in lean mode and has the escape-hatch link on its first slide.

**Why no segment is included twice in one deck.** The segment files contain R chunks with labels, and knitr refuses a duplicate label, so each deck includes each segment at most once.

**Rebuilding a deck.** Edit the segment files for content, or the deck file for order and framing, and render the deck on its own (`quarto render slides/housing-short.qmd`). A change to a shared segment needs every deck that includes it rendered again (`grep -l "shared/_x.qmd" slides/*.qmd`). The project render fails at its final move step on this machine, so decks are rendered one at a time.

## The housing-audit case

The housing-audit case is taught in a short session and in one day. The short session runs in the browser lab alone, in two halves of about seventy-five minutes: nothing is installed, nothing is sent to the class chart and nothing is preregistered. The three one-day focuses are taught mainly in the browser lab, with the workspace as an option. In Task 3 each participant chooses which of the analysts to reproduce; the four who recorded a statistic reproduce exactly from the public file, and P9W8Y, who recorded none, can be rerun but not matched. The [run sheet of the case](housing-guide.qmd) has the timings of the short session and of each focus of the day, the preparation that each format asks of participants, the expected numbers, the checks before the day and the order of what to cut.

## Self-study

The self-study track takes the housing-audit case in five stages, with the companion modules between the tasks, and ends on a project of each participant's own; a semester course can follow the same route in class. Its pages contain their own compression notes, written to the reader, because no facilitator is there to apply them, and the [facilitator guide](housing-guide.qmd#run-self-study) holds the time that each step of each stage asks. What the facilitator can still do for a self-study cohort is keep the live results pipeline running between deliveries, so that a result submitted alone appears on the Multiverse page of the case ([`facilitator/live-results-setup.md`](https://github.com/CodeMoreh/ar4ds-eu/blob/main/facilitator/live-results-setup.md) in the repository of the EU-frames site).

**The class chart.** The chart of the case is on its Multiverse page, and it reads only the rows of this case from the results Form that the cases of the course share. The labels of the housing-audit case carry the case word after the tag (`explore: [amber-otter-42] housing …`). The workspace keeps its tag in `.class-tag`, so ask a cohort to choose one nickname and to pass it as `nickname = "..."` every time. The chart keeps the rows of earlier deliveries until the sheet is cleared.
